clue.text: Revolutionary with that Parisian banner of revolution seen at end of race

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine-born guerrilla, is crosswords' stock revolutionary
que is the French word for that, as a Parisian would say it
the red flag is the traditional emblem of socialist and communist uprising

explanation.surface: A rebel carries a French revolutionary banner that is spotted as a race finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' simply joins the pieces. 'Revolutionary' and 'revolution' suggest a reversal, but nothing is turned: one is Che Guevara, the other describes a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: The black-and-white squared cloth is waved as the winner crosses the line in motor sport, so it is a thing spotted when a contest finishes.

clue.text: Rider looking exhausted and unwell

definitions.meaning: the middle name of the Victorian novelist who wrote King Solomon's Mines and She, standing here for his surname
gaunt and drawn in the face from tiredness or illness

explanation.surface: A horseman appears worn out and sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rider' looks like someone on horseback; it is the novelist H. Rider ..., known by that middle name.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the surname of the author Sir Henry Rider and an adjective for a gaunt, drawn appearance.

clue.text: No rivers in excavation wharf

indicators.note: no rivers tells you the letters for rivers are absent from the word for excavation

parts.note: a quarry is an open pit dug for stone
R is the map abbreviation for river, so two rivers are RR

explanation.surface: A dockside dug out without any waterways running through it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface runs 'excavation wharf' together as if one thing; the excavation is a stone pit, and 'No' strips both river letters from it, with 'in' only saying where they were.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: both are landing places where ships tie up to load and unload.

clue.text: Allow in French championship

parts.note: en is the French word for in
a sporting title is a championship, as in winning the league title

explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to give someone the right to something is to permit them to have it.

clue.text: Morally correct lie cath fabricated

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

clue.text: Deer had fine beard

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
the awn is the bristly beard on an ear of barley or other grass

explanation.surface: A stag sporting a handsome set of whiskers.

clue.text: A competitor, about mid-afternoon, coming

explanation.walkthrough: 'mid' takes the central letter R of afternoon, and 'about' wraps RIVAL round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a noun: the advent or appearance of someone, as in awaiting the guest's appearance.

clue.text: Does it tell you who is doing the royal rounds?

definitions.text: Does it tell you who is doing the royal rounds?

parts.words: Does it tell you who is doing the royal rounds?
parts.note: the daily official report of the British royal family's engagements, published in newspapers; rounds hints at the ring-shaped sense of its second word

explanation.definitionFit: The daily published record of royal engagements literally reports which royals are out on duty, and its second word suggests rounds.

clue.text: Ringleader?

parts.note: split as ring leader: the top fighter in the roped square where prizefights take place, not the head of a gang

explanation.definitionFit: The title-holding prizefighter is whimsically the leading figure of the roped square.

clue.text: Us soldier originally from Oregon sat out with one taking part in drunken revel

definitions.text: one taking part in drunken revel

indicators.note: originally from says the soldier has the state at his origin, so the state's letters come first

parts.note: OR is the US postal abbreviation for Oregon
GI is the usual term for an American serviceman

indicators.note: out, in the sense of astray or wrong, tells you the letters of sat are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An American serviceman from the Pacific Northwest skipped duty alongside a boozy party-goer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sat out' reads as skipping something, but 'out' jumbles the three letters into AST. 'originally from' is not a first-letter signal: it places the state ahead of the soldier. 'with' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A participant in a wild, drink-fuelled debauch is called this.

clue.text: No end of hawthorn growing wild near Bradford

indicators.note: a plant growing wild is untamed and disorderly, so the letters are rearranged
no end of means the final letter of hawthorn is left off

parts.note: taken as written, less its last letter

explanation.surface: Masses of thorny hedgerow shrubs run riot on the outskirts of a Yorkshire city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end of' drops the final N of hawthorn and 'growing wild' rearranges HAWTHOR. The definition is loose: a village close to Bradford in West Yorkshire, famous as home of the Bronte sisters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bronte sisters' moorland village lies a few miles west of that West Yorkshire city, so it is a place close by.

clue.text: Larry allowed to retain old coin

parts.note: the answer runs across the join of these two words

explanation.walkthrough: 'to retain' shows the answer sits inside 'Larry allowed', across the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a gold piece, also called a rose noble, struck in England from the fifteenth century.

clue.text: Flower store

definitions.meaning: a scented garden plant of the cabbage family, also called gillyflower
a supply of goods kept on hand for sale

explanation.definitionFit: Both a fragrant garden bloom and a supply of goods held by a shop.

clue.text: Move inside hesitantly to find egg

clue.text: Points out nose of pig

taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: The projecting muzzle of a hog is called this.

clue.text: Shrimp-like creatures take life seriously! That's about right

indicators.note: that is about says the preceding word goes around the letter for right

parts.note: to take life in grim earnest is to kill

explanation.surface: Tiny crustaceans are earnest about existence, and that seems roughly correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's about' wraps KILL round R. 'take life seriously' is a joke: not being earnest, but ending a life.
explanation.definitionFit: The small crustaceans that swarm in the oceans and feed whales resemble tiny prawns.

clue.text: Rotter enclosed note on rhythm

parts.note: cad and rotter are both dated British words for a dishonourable man
enc is the abbreviation written on a letter to show something is enclosed
E is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: A scoundrel slipped a memo about musical timing into the envelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' links the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the beat or measured flow of music or speech.

clue.text: Siren learning with the French individual

le is the French word for the

explanation.surface: An alarm goes off while someone studies with a person from France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the pieces. The siren is not an alarm but a mythical temptress: the Rhine maiden whose song lured sailors onto the rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the legendary Rhine enchantress who lured boatmen to destruction with her singing.

clue.text: New member annoyed courtier dropping ball

O looks like a ball

clue.text: Can vote out small amount of south American money

definitions.text: small amount of south American money

indicators.note: out, in the sense of wrong or astray, tells you the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: It is possible to vote down a tiny sum of Latin American cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges CAN and VOTE together.

clue.text: Strike north African on the way up to liquor shop

indicators.note: in a down entry, on the way up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: a Moor is a member of a north-west African Muslim people

explanation.surface: Hit a man from Morocco as he climbs the hill to the off-licence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way up' turns MOOR into ROOM in this down entry; 'to' links to the definition.

clue.text: A plant's emerging from shallow basin

explanation.walkthrough: 'emerging' rearranges A PLANTS; 'from' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural depression where seawater or brine evaporates and leaves mineral deposits.

clue.text: Different speed on foot

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Walking is a change of pace.
